questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A country with a high level of English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy as I was not sure of how the registration process would take place. But was very easy, once done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many rooms very available, they had many different kinds. Also en-suites, but you will never get them, as they are for the students staying longer than 1 term only.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could by a subscription to get 'free' food on campus twice a day. Seemed to be very affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Not much cleaning of common-areas is done, just once every 3 weeks by a cleaning lady. So aim to keep it clean yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All I had to do was to go to the Library to get signed in, using my passport and then receiving my Kent ID card. Then found my way to your accommodation to get my room keys. that was all. From there I only had to show up for classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much. Just had to ask around on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The Uni is very successful in meeting the students' wishes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the Library to get signed in and then find your way to your accommodation. once you get your Kent ID card and room keys, you're all set and done.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not very high in itself, the difficulty lies in the language barriers and working on a new examination structure as they do law exams very differently than DK.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Exams are essay based, meaning you write an article / essay about 4-5000 words upon a concrete issue or topic, that you pick yourself, out of 10 issues offered by the module convenor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Commercial Arbitration; Corporate Governance; International Law on Foreign Investments.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International focussed for sure, so the courses will be attractive for any employer to see on your CV.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Trains are ridiculously expensive due to privatisation. Domestic planes (i.e. RyanAir) is cheaper than trains. Busses are the cheapest transportation form.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: UK is generally 10-15% cheaper than DK, thus still being an expensive country for sure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various different societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel the whole country. Very different from DK.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The whole of UK. If it wasn't for the weather the UK would be a very exotic place with its beaches, cliffs and nature in general. Further, the cities are the more American-like than any other cities in EU, such as London and Liverpool. Also visit Scotland, the treasure of UK. Very diverse country in terms of its cities. Go to Kent to see the UK you see in BBC News and in Harry Potter, of these small houses with small gardens and ugly cars.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: UK is very much DK like, except the UK being more talkative, openminded and respectful. be ready for people talking to you at unexpected times.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies in aim to find mind a like people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: saying please at random times. Saying thank you to the bus driver was very weird for me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The talkativenesses, the open-mindedness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: UK is expensive. Be mindfull of the fact you have to be openminded to meeting new people, even if they might not necessarily look like the typical people you hang out with back at home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: being exposed to the talkativeness of UK.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Using the word please when ordering food.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
